proposal.root_problem: Refunds are failing at the payment stage due to invalid/malformed IBAN data (5/5 sampled payment-db refund_failures records show status FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT, E-01), causing customers whose refunds have genuinely failed — not merely lacking visible status — to repeatedly contact support and generate tickets, independent of agent response speed (median 2.0h vs 24h SLA across 900 tickets, E-02).
proposal.requested_solution: Build a chatbot so customers stop waiting for answers about refunds (SH-SUP initial request, CL-01).
symptoms: Customers report waiting for answers about refund status (SH-SUP claims CL-01/CL-02).
Sampled payment-db refund_failures records (5/5) show status FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT rather than a completed/resolved status (E-01).
Refund-related support contact persists despite support agents responding quickly (median 2.0h vs 24h SLA across 900 tickets, E-02).
causal_chain: Refund transactions enter payment processing carrying customer IBAN banking details (DA-PAY).
All 5 sampled payment-db refund_failures records show status FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT, indicating invalid/malformed IBAN data blocks payment completion (E-01).
Because the refund transaction genuinely fails at the payment stage rather than merely lacking visible status, the customer's refund does not complete.
The customer contacts support about the unresolved refund, generating a ticket within the refund process (P-REF).

Although agent response is fast (median 2.0h vs 24h SLA across 900 tickets, E-02), the underlying payment failure remains unresolved, so the customer continues to perceive 'waiting' — for the refund to succeed, not for an answer channel.

proposal.summary: The initial request (CL-01, SH-SUP) was to build a chatbot so customers stop waiting for refund answers. Testing this against evidence (E-01: 5/5 sampled payment-db refund_failures show FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT; E-02: ticket-db shows 2.0h median response vs 24h SLA across 900 tickets) showed the real problem (PD-1) is that refunds genuinely fail at the payment stage due to malformed IBANs, not a missing self-service channel or slow agents. The DEFINE gate returned CONDITIONAL_PASS, deferring the high-criticality population-representativeness unknown as a verification obligation. The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION (no holds), covering confirm_iban_failure_mechanism:DA-PAY and notify_customers_of_failed_refund:DA-TCK; the population-scale analysis was excluded pending its before-release VOB, and two before-production VOBs (bank-api reversibility, IBAN malformation cause) remain open but did not block this release.
key_points: Original request: SH-SUP's CL-01 asked for a chatbot so customers stop waiting for refund answers.
Evidence E-01 (payment-db.refund_failures, F-01) shows all 5 sampled records have status FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT, supporting H-IBAN-FORMAT-FAILURE and rejecting H-NO-SELF-SERVICE-CHANNEL.
Evidence E-02 (ticket-db.response_times, F-02) shows median response 2.0h vs 24h SLA across 900 tickets, rejecting H-TICKET-HANDLING-BOTTLENECK (slow agents are not the cause).
SH-SUP's follow-up claim CL-02/E-03 restated the chatbot framing without new evidence and did not engage with E-01/E-02; it is flagged as matching SH-SUP's documented bias toward speed-framing.
DEFINE gate result was CONDITIONAL_PASS, deferring U-POPULATION-REPRESENTATIVENES (HIGH criticality) to VOB-U-POPULATION-REPRESENTATIVENES.

Release decision: RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION, hold list empty; released scope is confirm_iban_failure_mechanism:DA-PAY and notify_customers_of_failed_refund:DA-TCK (work items W-WI-1, W-WI-2 marked DONE).
analyze_refund_failure_population:DA-PAY was excluded from release because VOB-U-POPULATION-REPRESENTATIVENES is required BEFORE_RELEASE and remains OPEN.

VOB-R-2 (bank-api DEGRADED/ACCESS_DENIED reversibility, tied to a logged HOLD with stop_reason NOT_TRANSIENT) and VOB-R-3 (cause of malformed IBANs) are open but only required BEFORE_PRODUCTION, so they did not block this release.
limitations_explained: Conclusions rest on only 5 sampled refund_failures records; DA-PAY completeness is UNKNOWN, so findings are provisional until the full population is checked (ties to VOB-U-POPULATION-REPRESENTATIVENES, required before release).
The release does not fix refunds already stuck in FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT, because bank-api is DEGRADED and restoring access was not feasible in contest time.
The analyze_refund_failure_population:DA-PAY scope item is excluded from this release pending resolution of the open population-representativeness VOB.
It is unresolved what share of the 900 tickets (E-02) are refund-related (U-TICKET-VOLUME-ATTRIBUTION), which limits precision in measuring the impact of the failed-refund notification.
Whether the bank-api DEGRADED/ACCESS_DENIED state is reversible, and on what timeline, is unresolved (VOB-R-2); it is tracked as required before production, not before this release.
The root cause of IBAN malformation (customer entry error, data migration bug, or bank format change) is unresolved (VOB-R-3); also required before production, not before this release.
